question: Satellites count every flash of lightning on Earth. About how many flashes occur worldwide each second?
answer: About 44. Satellite optical sensors, watching for years, measured a global mean of 44 flashes a second, well over a billion a year, mostly over land in the tropics. Anyone counting from one town sees only a few storms a year and guesses far lower.
move: Your own patch is a small sample; look for someone who counted everywhere.
trap: Judging by the few storms seen from one town.
source: Christian and others, Journal of Geophysical Research, 2003
reference: Christian et al., Global frequency and distribution of lightning as observed from space by the Optical Transient Detector, Journal of Geophysical Research, 2003
